subject: SEI-B7 outcome-informed cognitive routing policy

architecturalPosition.learningTarget: route efficacy by caller-owned problem class

selectionRule: route escalation must be at or above caller-owned minimum
cognitive sufficient rate must meet required floor
firstSlice.activationBoundary: BuildCandidate stores an immutable candidate snapshot but does not change the active policy. Activate(version) is explicit; activating an older snapshot performs rollback.
firstSlice.provenanceBoundary: Each route-efficacy aggregate retains observed-policy-version counts and sorted evidence refs.

syntheticFixtures.observation: A lower-escalation route can become a candidate when explicit assessed evidence meets the caller-owned floor, without implicit activation.
When the lower route misses the required cognitive-efficacy floor, the static route is preserved.
Execution failures attached to not-assessed records are tracked separately and do not become cognitive insufficiency; minimum assessed evidence still blocks adaptation.
Perfect synthetic efficacy cannot move routing below a caller-owned escalation floor; a route below the floor is not counted as avoidable escalation in replay.

syntheticFixtures.routeOutcomes: local-slm and general-llm both sufficient in both cases
syntheticFixtures.observation: In this synthetic slice, the candidate reduces escalation while preserving success.
A holdout shift can make the adapted lower route fail where the static route succeeds. Past efficacy is not treated as a future guarantee.
Rollback reproduces the prior route because snapshots are immutable and activation changes only the active-version pointer.

localVerification.sourceMethod: The three branch source files policy.go, replay.go, and policy_test.go were retrieved from the private GitHub branch, decoded into a temporary module, locally gofmt-normalized, and executed. The local go.mod only changed the Go directive from 1.25 to 1.23.

benchmark.name: BenchmarkBuildCandidate
benchmark.note: Builds a new store and candidate from a 215-record synthetic evidence set. This is local Go 1.23 evaluation performance, not production or Go 1.25 evidence.

localVerification.independentFixtureCheck: A separate standalone Go reconstruction reproduced the candidate selections and the positive/shift replay metrics before the branch-source test.

stopLines: route success != Recommendation or Decision correctness
notVerified: human or validator process that assigns sufficient / insufficient outcomes
selection-bias correction when only executed routes have outcomes
statistical confidence bounds beyond minimum observation count
policy expiry / drift detection / automatic rollback criteria
real latency, privacy, energy, and cost tradeoffs
Product Value, Operational, Adoption, or Outcome Evidence
